title: Ukraine's 2023 summer counteroffensive begins in the south and east
body:
Ukraine's 2023 counteroffensive is dated by the Institute for the Study of War to 4 June 2023, when Russia reported thwarted Ukrainian attacks and wider Ukrainian operations began. Ukraine did not announce a start date, and Western media reported the offensive on 8 June. The main effort was in the south in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, aimed at the Melitopol and Berdiansk directions under commander Oleksandr Tarnavskyi. A second axis near Bakhmut in Donetsk Oblast was commanded by Oleksandr Syrskyi, and some units later shifted to the Dnieper sector in Kherson Oblast.

Of twelve planned brigades, nine were trained and equipped by the United States and three were trained in Ukraine. Leopard 2 tanks and Bradley fighting vehicles advanced near Orikhiv on 9-10 June, and five Leopard 2 tanks were knocked out in one week, all by Russian FPV drones. Ukraine recaptured Staromaiorske on 26 July and announced the capture of Urozhaine on 16 August. Urban combat in Robotyne began on 11 August, and troops entered the northwestern outskirts of Verbove on 30 August.

By October 2023 the objectives of reaching Melitopol and Tokmak and the Sea of Azov had not been met. Ukraine recaptured 14 villages in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk oblasts, with a pre-war population of about 5,000, and captured over 370 square kilometres. Valerii Zaluzhnyi described the war as a stalemate in early November. By early December several outlets considered the offensive stalled or failed.
